issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual specification) defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning a boolean (it explicitly states the method should return true if milking was successful, false otherwise), but the provided solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a String and the concrete classes (Goat, Seal) implement it returning Strings. This mismatch in the return type for a core interface is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about the expected signature and prevent them from implementing/compiling code consistent with both the specification and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable interface return type across all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnMilk() returns String (and clarify the expected string format), or (B) change the solution and template to declare messageOnMilk() returning boolean and update Goat and Seal to return a boolean (and adjust any code/tests that consume the method). Ensure templates, tests, and examples (Main) use the same signature so students can implement without discrepancy.
